messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

Following up on this conversation, I wish to ask for clarification as to what each level of hierarchy in the poppr AMOVA output is actually calculating. In my particular study design, I have individuals nested within sites, and these sites are nested within two regions. I have read the poppr documentation, but I am unclear as to how "heterozygosities within genotypes" are actually being calculated. To my understanding, heterozygosity is determined at the individual level, so how are heterozygosities within individuals being calculated -- what is the level of analyses here? Unfortunately, the R output is not clearly providing insights in this regard. I understand this syntax is being inherited from ade4, but the description regarding genotypes being split into haplotypes on the poppr documentation is not in line with how my data is structured.

Likewise, in running the randtest command, my output presents 3 tests: (1) variation within samples, (2) variation between samples, and (3) variations between regions. My AMOVA has each site nested within region (~region/site). In this case, is the variation between samples referring to differences between individuals at a single site? For the variation between regions, is this then comparing the variation between my two regions?

Thank you in advance for your time and guidance -- poppr has been a wonderful package to use in my research.

Best regards,

Victoria

On Thursday, August 15, 2019 at 11:28:35 AM UTC-4 Brian Knaus wrote:
> Hi Raj,
>
> The data contained in VCF data and a genlight object are very different. I don't think there is a good way to convert a genlight object into VCF data. I would suggest reading your vcf data into R and perform any filtering or data cleaning on the vcfR object. You can then fork your workflow into two paths. One path you can write the vcfR object to a VCF file and use vcftools to convert the VCF file into plink format. The second path would convert the vcfR object into a genlight object for analysis in adegenet and poppr.
>

messages.body_plain:
This may help:

 from the "On Within Individual Variance" from https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/poppr.amova.html:

> Heterozygosities within genotypes are sources of variation from within individuals and can be quantified in AMOVA. When within = TRUE, poppr will split genotypes into haplotypes with the function make_haplotypes() <https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/make_haplotypes-method.html> and use those to calculate within-individual variance. No estimation of phase is made. This acts much like the default settings for AMOVA in the Arlequin software package. Within individual variance will not be calculated for haploid individuals or dominant markers as the haplotypes cannot be split further. Setting within = FALSE uses the euclidean distance of the allele frequencies within each individual. Note: within = TRUE is incompatible with filter = TRUE. In this case, within will be set to FALSE

Dear All

I am quite new to R programming as well as using the package, "poppr". I have a dataset of 10 loci from 58 individuals from 3 populations which I have imported to RStudio as an xlsx file. I used the same command as the one for the dataset example of nancycats which reads as nan-geno <- genotype_curve(nancycats) from the paper "Produce a genotype accumulation curve" by Zhian N. I then used the command provided by RStudio to generate a genind object of my file. I did manage to do that, however, the genind object generated could not be used to create the genotype curve since no data frame was generated under the optional content and it read as:
 //optional content
-empty-

Now I am wondering, where could I have made the mistake. Could it be that I did not convert me xlsx file into csv before the import or could it be that I only used the columns of the loci? However, I did troubleshoot to check and I imported the entire dataset with population names, sample codes, etc and got an error when I tried to convert it into genind.
I would really appreciate your assistance on this and I thank you wholeheartedly in advance.

Kindest regards
Martin

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] 'pair.ia' NA's
messages.body_plain:
There's a lot going on here so I'm going to answer this the best I can, but I make no promises that it will actually answer your question.

First, the last chapter of my dissertation handles factors that could influence values of the index of association. You can read the dissertation version <https://zkamvar.github.io/dissertation/5-factors-influencing-inference-of-clonality-in-diploid-populations.html#> or you can read the (pdf) version that we intended to publish, but never did <https://github.com/zkamvar/clonal-inference-simulations/raw/master/manuscript/clonal-inference.pdf> (largely due to my moving out of the field), which demonstrates why you can achieve severely negative values of the index of association with an ostensibly clonal population.

Second, you will receive negative values of the index of association looking at a single pair of loci when one of those loci is monomorphic since the observed and expected variance of that locus will be zero, leading the value of the denominator of rd to be zero and thus leading rd to be not a number. With Ia, the denominator is the sum of the expected variance for all loci, so that value will simply be zero, which makes sense because a locus with no variance can not tell you any information about linkage with another locus.

Hope that helps.
Best,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] AMOVA with single stratum data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Martin,

You can assign a single stratum to your data by using the `strata(myData) <- dataFrame` syntax.
If you already have a population factor for your data (you can check this by running `nPop(myData) > 0` to make sure you have a population set), then you can assign the strata with that.

Here's an example using the nancycats data set. I've highlighted the line that sets the strata in bold:
library("poppr")
data(nancycats) # embedded data set of cat colonies from Nancy, FR
strata(nancycats) <- data.frame(colony = pop(nancycats)) # create a strata from the one population factor
poppr.amova(nancycats, ~colony) # run AMOVA, using the colony as the single stratum
